key_insight: End-to-end driving models can fail in closed loop because their intermediate waypoints are often physically inconsistent, so the paper proposes preserving the predicted endpoint while repairing the trajectory geometry.
engineering_relevance: A lightweight, no-map postprocessing layer can be dropped between many waypoint-based policies and controllers to improve closed-loop driving without retraining.
method: Anchor the plan to the vehicle’s executed history.
Keep the policy’s predicted endpoint fixed.
Reshape intermediate waypoints to make the trajectory more feasible and controller-friendly.
evidence_signal: Across two closed-loop simulators, ECO improved all six evaluated policies, including VaVAM on HUGSIM from 18.1 to 31.0 HD-Score and scene-score gains on AlpaSim for VaVAM and DiffusionDrive.
watch_item: Because ECO modifies only the trajectory geometry, its benefit may depend on the controller and on how severely the base policy violates motion limits; it does not add map or privileged-state awareness.
paper_title: Guiding End-to-End Driving Models with Endpoint-Constrained Trajectory Optimization
